root_cause.text: PR #4471 deployed to ledger-service 23 minutes ago, touching src/db/connection-pool.ts
root_cause.author: Ben Ortiz

memory.lesson: ledger-service ran a fixed Postgres pool of 20 connections. A retry storm from checkout-api saturated it and every caller queued on acquire, so p99 latency climbed while CPU stayed flat -- the signature of pool exhaustion rather than compute pressure. Fix was to raise the pool ceiling to 60 and add a per-caller bulkhead in src/db/connection-pool.ts so one noisy upstream cannot consume the whole pool. Check pool saturation before chasing CPU whenever latency rises with flat utilisation.

fix.body:
Symptom: p99 latency climbing while CPU stays flat, acquire timeouts in logs, waiters queueing on the connection pool.
1. Check pool saturation: pg_stat_activity count vs the configured ceiling in src/db/connection-pool.ts.
2. If saturated, raise the ceiling and restart rolling. Do not restart all replicas.
3. Identify the noisy upstream from per-caller acquire metrics and rate limit it.
4. Add or verify the per-caller bulkhead so one upstream cannot take the whole pool.
Escalate to Payments Platform if the ledger balance endpoint is affected.

nodes.lesson: Scoring model rollouts had no shadow-mode gate. All model versions now run in shadow against production traffic for 24h before any live share.
template-renderer shipped a breaking template schema without a version negotiation. Renderer responses are now versioned and the fan-out worker falls back to the previous template on schema mismatch.

ledger-service ran a fixed Postgres pool of 20 connections. A retry storm from checkout-api saturated it and every caller queued on acquire, so p99 latency climbed while CPU stayed flat -- the signature of pool exhaustion rather than compute pressure. Fix was to raise the pool ceiling to 60 and add a per-caller bulkhead in src/db/connection-pool.ts so one noisy upstream cannot consume the whole pool. Check pool saturation before chasing CPU whenever latency rises with flat utilisation.
Index rebuilds had no rate limit and ran on a cron that overlapped peak hours. Rebuilds are now token-bucket limited and scheduled off-peak.
Synchronous replication was configured on one replica only. Promotion picked an async replica. Quorum commit across two replicas is now required.

maxmemory-policy was allkeys-lru across shared cache namespaces, so a batch job filled redis-cache and evicted live session keys. Namespace isolation with per-prefix memory budgets prevented recurrence.
The rate refresher failed silently when the upstream returned 304. Staleness is now an alerting metric rather than a log line.

args.lesson: checkout-api p99 latency breached threshold with flat CPU: connection pool exhausted, acquire timeouts, waiters queueing. That is pool exhaustion, not compute pressure. Cause was PR #4471 deployed to ledger-service 2 hops upstream, touching src/db/connection-pool.ts. Pooled client reuse in the hot path reduced the effective pool ceiling, so callers queued on acquire and the latency surfaced at the customer-facing service rather than at the service that changed. Fix: raise the pool ceiling and add a per-caller bulkhead. For this signature, check pool saturation before CPU.
